# Report: *A Modest Proposal* (Swift, 1729)

## 1. The question, frozen

The title and opening put one question central, so I freeze that: **how to rear and provide for the roughly 120,000 poor children born yearly in Ireland, so they stop being a burden and become "useful members of the commonwealth."** Range: this kingdom, this year, the poor. Asked: what produces relief, from causes.

But this is a parody. Swift answers that question in bad faith to indict a different one – how the ruling discourse treats the Irish poor. I hold the surface question still, mark it as the one under test, and note where the real work lies.

## 2. The explanation in parts (owner's words)

P1 premise: the children are "a very great additional grievance," a burden. P2 count: 1.5m souls, 120,000 children. P3 age and weight: one year old, 28 pounds. P4 food: "delicious nourishing and wholesome," stewed, roasted, baked, boiled. P5 breeding: 20,000 kept, one male to four females. P6 money: 2s cost, 10s carcass, 8s profit, £50,000 gain. P7 refinements: gloves, boots. P8 advantages: fewer Papists, marriage inducement, tavern custom. P9 the dismissal list: tax absentees, buy native goods, landlord mercy. P10 persona: no children, no self-interest.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| P1 burden | **Borrowed** | Rests on the landlords'/English account of the poor, named not tested here. Ironically the load-bearing part. |
| P2 count | **Fitted** | Mimics projector arithmetic; tuned to look exact. Swap the figures, nothing moves. |
| P3 age/weight | **Held** (by the profit job: fattest at a year, mother fit to work again); the exact 28 lbs is **loose**. |
| P4 menu | **Loose** | "Roasted" for "boiled" changes nothing; the held thing is only "edible commodity." |
| P5 ratio | **Loose** | One male to four, three, or five – nothing moves. Parodies stock-breeding. |
| P6 money | **Held if** the "cheap, easy, no expence" job is the real one; figures themselves fitted. |
| P7 gloves/boots | **Loose** detail doing one job: renders the poor as raw material. |
| P8 advantages | **Held**; "lessen the Papists" is held and is the concealed aim. |
| P9 dismissal list | **Held** – the hinge: names the real remedies only to foreclose them. |
| P10 persona | **Borrowed/fixed** – the projector's pose, set by the genre, not tested. |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Had the poor been prospering, no scheme. The Proposal fits any outcome where the poor are a burden to be reduced; it even owns depopulation as "one principal design." It is held only by P1.

**Direction.** It runs backwards. It starts from the wished result – a clean, profitable, Papist-free Ireland – and invents a cause. Poke the cause (cook the children): the result moves, in the fiction. Poke the result (the real expedients): Swift blocks it – "let no man talk to me of these."

**Answer in the starting points.** Yes. "Burden," "grievance," "useful," "breeders." The conclusion – the poor are consumable material – is already sitting in the opening under the word *useful*.

**Jobs' origin.** P1 is the owner's (the ruling discourse). Swift adds the rest as parody; his own jobs are marked **added**.

**Pairs that pull.** P8's "care and tenderness of mothers," mares in foal, sows farrowing, pulls hard against the wholesale slaughter. Swift makes the joint visible on purpose.

**Catch-alls.** None. His tightness is that no bin exists – every horror is named. The "no other expedients" list is the anti-catch-all.

**What the change list leaves out.** The moral question (help rather than consume) and the working poor, handled by conscription – "happily delivered from the evils to come."

**Rival.** P9's real remedies. What tells them apart? Not logic, but willingness: the honest ones are "vain, idle, visionary" because nobody attempts them; the Proposal is cheap, easy, "full in our own power." The difference is cost, and that is the accusation.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

As a *proposal*, very little: the menu, the ratios, the counts are loose by design, imitating the projector's slackness. That looseness is load-bearing as parody. As *satire*, it is already tight, because it is held by P1 – the real discourse it mirrors. The single job that does the most work is P1. Remove it and the whole collapses, which is Swift's whole point: the discourse has already eaten the parents ("already devoured"), so eating the children merely finishes the meal.

## 6. What this does not show

Hard to vary is not true. A monstrous scheme can be internally tight, and this one nearly is. The method has no ethics meter and no taste meter. Passing here licenses nothing.

## 7. One next step

Hand a sincere projector of 1729 the swap: replace "child" with "bacon." If the argument still runs, the discourse never needed the child – only the commodity. That swap is the test Swift built, and he made it almost impossible to fail.
